title: Ethereum whale moves $57.88M as outflows deepen — Can ETH defend $2,400?
summary: Ethereum's whale transfers and exchange outflows contrasted with bearish indicators.
content: An Ethereum whale has transferred $57.88 million as exchange outflows continue to deepen. The significant movement of funds comes amid a mix of whale activity and bearish market indicators, raising questions about whether ETH can successfully defend the critical $2,400 support level.
content_ta: எக்ஸ்சேஞ்ச் வெளிப்பாடுகள் அதிகரித்து வரும் நிலையில், ஒரு Ethereum வேல் $57.88 மில்லியன் மதிப்பை மாற்றியுள்ளது. இந்த பெரிய அளவிலான நிதி நகர்வு மற்றும் கரடி சந்தை குறிகளால், ETH அதன் முக்கியமான $2,400 ஆதரவு விலையைத் தக்கவைக்குமா என்ற கேள்வி எழுந்துள்ளது.

title: Ben Horowitz says AI fast takeoff is unlikely as key conditions go unmet
summary:
AI's growth is constrained by resource and infrastructure limits, impacting investment strategies and delaying self-improvement breakthroughs.
The post Ben Horowitz says AI fast takeoff is unlikely as key conditions go unmet appeared first on Crypto Briefing.
content: Venture capitalist Ben Horowitz stated that a rapid 'fast takeoff' for artificial intelligence is unlikely because crucial infrastructure and resource conditions remain unmet. These physical and logistical limits constrain AI growth, affecting current investment strategies and pushing back potential self-improvement breakthroughs.
content_ta: AI-யின் விரைவான வளர்ச்சிக்கான 'fast takeoff' சாத்தியமில்லை என்று Ben Horowitz தெரிவித்துள்ளார். தேவையான உள்கட்டமைப்பு மற்றும் வளங்கள் இன்னும் பூர்த்தி செய்யப்படாததே இதற்குக் காரணம். இந்த எல்லைகள் AI வளர்ச்சியைக் கட்டுப்படுத்தி, முதலீட்டு உத்திகளைப் பாதிக்கின்றன.

title: Circle Reveals $819 Million USDC Payouts As Stablecoin Economics Come Under Scrutiny
summary: TL;DR: Circle says it generated roughly $1.4 billion in first-half 2026 revenue while spending $819 million on distribution partners and related costs. The disclosure highlights the expense of building a widely used stablecoin payment network. Circle’s USDC business is generating substantial revenue, but its latest disclosures show how much of that income is needed to support distribution and infrastructure. The stablecoin issuer reported approximately $1.4 billion of revenue in the first half of 2026. It said around $819 million went to partners and transaction-related costs, while another $473 million supported operational, compliance and technology spending. That leaves a much smaller proportion of revenue as retained profit than the headline size of USDC might suggest. The Economics Of A Digital Dollar Circle holds reserves backing USDC in cash and highly liquid financial instruments. Those assets can produce interest income, creating an important revenue stream for the issuer. But USDC’s usefulness depends on its presence across exchanges, wallets, payment services and other financial applications. Those distribution arrangements can be expensive. Coinbase is among Circle’s most important commercial partners, reflecting its role in making the stablecoin accessible to users. As NewsBTC has previously explained, USDC aims to maintain its value against the dollar while remaining transferable across supported networks. Competition Raises The Stakes New stablecoin issuers and conventional financial institutions are entering the market. They will compete not only on the reliability of their reserves but also on distribution, redemption and cost. Circle’s revenue also depends partly on interest rates. Lower yields on reserves could compress income even if USDC’s circulation remains relatively strong. The latest figures reveal an important part of the stablecoin business: issuing the digital dollar may be only the first step. The partners enabling people to use it can command a considerable share of the economic value. Written by the News Desk and edited by Samuel Rae.
content: Circle disclosed generating roughly $1.4 billion in revenue for the first half of 2026, alongside $819 million in USDC distribution and partner payouts. The figures highlight the substantial expenses required to maintain a stablecoin payment network, including infrastructure, compliance, and key commercial partnerships such as Coinbase, amid rising competition in the digital asset market.
content_ta: 2026-ஆம் ஆண்டின் முதல் பாதியில் Circle நிறுவனம் சுமார் 1.4 பில்லியன் டாலர் வருவாய் ஈட்டியுள்ளதாகவும், USDC விநியோகம் மற்றும் கூட்டாளர் செலவுகளுக்காக 819 மில்லியன் டாலர் செலவிடப்பட்டுள்ளதாகவும் தெரிவித்துள்ளது. டிஜிட்டல் சொத்து சந்தையில் அதிகரித்து வரும் போட்டியின் மத்தியில், Coinbase போன்ற முக்கிய வணிகக் கூட்டாண்மைகள் மற்றும் உள்கட்டமைப்புச் செலவுகள் ஸ்டேபிள்காயின் நெட்வொர்க்கை பராமரிக்க எவ்வளவு அவசியமாகிறது என்பதை இந்த விவரங்கள் காட்டுகின்றன.

title: Microsoft plans to pay Anthropic over $2B a year to keep Copilot competitive
summary:
Microsoft's investment in Anthropic highlights the competitive AI landscape, emphasizing strategic partnerships to enhance product performance.
The post Microsoft plans to pay Anthropic over $2B a year to keep Copilot competitive appeared first on Crypto Briefing.
content: Microsoft is reportedly planning to make a massive financial investment of over $2 billion annually in Anthropic. This strategic move is aimed at keeping the company's Copilot product competitive within the rapidly evolving artificial intelligence landscape. The collaboration highlights how major technology firms are forming powerful partnerships to enhance their AI capabilities and maintain market advantage.

Copilot தயாரிப்பை போட்டித்தன்மையுடன் வைத்திருக்க இந்த வியூக நடவடிக்கை உதவும் என எதிர்பார்க்கப்படுகிறது. AI துறையில் முன்னணியில் இருக்க முன்னணி தொழில்நுட்ப நிறுவனங்கள் இதுபோன்று கூட்டு சேர்வதை இது காட்டுகிறது.

title: Bitget restricts access to Russia, Belarus, Kazakhstan, and sanctioned entities
summary: Bitget has tightened its internal compliance to fight illicit flows.
content: Cryptocurrency exchange Bitget has restricted user access from Russia, Belarus, Kazakhstan, and certain sanctioned entities. The platform implemented these measures to tighten internal compliance and combat illicit financial flows. This decision reflects the growing regulatory pressure on digital asset exchanges to strengthen security and adhere to international standards regarding restricted jurisdictions.

title: CoreWeave, Broadcom, Verizon among nine companies objecting to tokenized trading of their shares on OKXICE
summary: Applied Optoelectronics told the WSJ it objected because it was unsure how tokenization would affect its stock price, liquidity and volatility.
content: CoreWeave, Broadcom, Verizon, and several other companies have objected to the tokenized trading of their shares on OKXICE. Applied Optoelectronics stated it raised objections because of uncertainties regarding how stock tokenization could impact its share price, market liquidity, and volatility.
